texts.label: Lord Maltravers to Ormonde, 13 Sept 1634 and 22 Jan 1634/5 (HMC Ormonde I pp. 28-29)
texts.summary: Letter 1: the Earl of Kildare came to England because he was angry with the Lord Deputy (Wentworth), and the King refused to see him because he brought no letters from the Lord Deputy. Letter 2: Sir Piers Crosby's position is likely to go worse; the Lord Deputy has written to Secretary Coke in praise of Ormonde, particularly for his good carriage in the Parliament, and on his motion Ormonde is to be made a councillor. Both match Wentworth's dispatches in Knowler's Strafforde's Letters (1739).
